report.symptom: After the first 4P one-shot, the floating one-shot button stays disabled when the local board is manually playable.
report.user_clarification: The affected control is the floating one-shot button. Diagnostics were copied later, not at the disabled playable board.
limits: The current board was absent at copy time; its zero fields do not describe the playable board when the button was disabled.
The log proves local swap acknowledgements and release, not peer/server synchronization.
Disabled-time network flags were not captured. The native branch identifies a concrete source defect capable of causing this symptom; device confirmation of the fix is pending.

method: Read-only IDA decompilation and original/current instruction bytes; static source/data review only. No game, fixture, compiler, generator, test suite or CI execution.

evidence.finding: After a moved local gesture releases, native code ORs 2 into impl+0xafe70. The separate resolve byte at impl+0x9299a is set to 1; phase may still be 2.
The native input precheck detects network flag bit 1 and takes a competitive-specific path. A submitted flag is not universally a prohibition on later orb input.

sub_100542b74(1) selects only 8P. A 4P return of zero branches to the return epilogue without clearing impl+0xafe70. 8P may enter phase 69, clears the flags, and initializes its following board separately.
Argument 0 recognizes categories 10 and 11; argument 1 recognizes category 10 only. This distinguishes the 4P early return from the 8P flag reset.
Native phase-2 initialization clears the resolve byte. The source still requires phase 2, resolvePending=0, local view/seat, valid active clock, connection, settled board and quiet input.

change.effect: A fresh eligible 4P board with flags 3 or 0x23 can expose the one-shot button and bind a new explicit gesture. Resolution still disables it. No native flag is cleared or written.

diagnostics.metadata_only_release: A valid phase-2 release can contain only identity/drag metadata. Preserve observedBoard unless every board token was read; zero orb values alone remain valid fire orbs.
diagnostics.current_readiness: onceReadiness includes frame/feature/busy/opening gates, current read reason and age, board/leader/time eligibility and native multiplayer fields.
diagnostics.runtime_readiness: runtimeReadiness includes final canOnce/canExecute/canStart, account/application/storage/config gates and pending team operations.
diagnostics.retained_readiness: At most 16 distinct multiplayer readiness observations, captured when the UI/session snapshot is requested and retained after scene exit. This is not a per-frame trace. Clock ticks and route swaps do not independently add entries.
diagnostics.privacy: No account IDs, container paths, process pointers or raw device log are added to the repository.

coverage: 4P accepts retained bit 1 only with active bit 0; 3P/8P still reject it.
Resolution, remote view, missing active bit and send/pass/sync/terminal flags remain rejected.
Successful gesture, phase-2 metadata-only release, fresh local board and a second explicit one-shot in each mode.
3P waits through other seats; 4P keeps its turn serial and submitted flag; 8P returns through reset flags.
New-board availability cannot auto-arm or reuse an old gesture; second begin and release are independent.
Metadata-only release preserves the real last board and records the observed multiplayer flags.
Readiness history is bounded, ignores unchanged clock ticks and remains available after scene exit.
Floating control changes from completed/waiting to ready and only another tap invokes the next action.

static_checks.limitation: Source/data consistency and lexical checks passed; written regression cases have not run, and the reported device symptom still requires confirmation.

pending: Authorized model/session/native/overlay test run and iPhoneOS build from the same source.
4P device: first one-shot, next playable board, button recovery, second explicit shot, and third board without automatic input.
3P local-turn handoff and 8P next-board regression, countdown end, disconnection and manual interruption.
Check onceReadiness, runtimeReadiness and onceReadinessHistory if the button is still disabled; disabled-time evidence is required to attribute any remaining blocker.
Peer synchronization and server acceptance remain unverified.
